---
title: "AnalogIntervalPeak (TransformsV2)"
---

## Overview

`AnalogIntervalPeak` finds the maximum or minimum analog sample within each
interval (or between interval starts) and emits the peak times as a
`DigitalEventSeries`.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Registry name | `AnalogIntervalPeak` |
| Container signature | `(DigitalIntervalSeries, AnalogTimeSeries) → DigitalEventSeries` |
| Category | Signal Processing / Time Series |

Source files:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/TransformsV2/algorithms/AnalogIntervalPeak/AnalogIntervalPeak.hpp` | Params + API |
| `src/TransformsV2/algorithms/AnalogIntervalPeak/AnalogIntervalPeak.cpp` | Implementation |
| `src/DataManager/transforms/AnalogTimeSeries/Analog_Interval_Peak/analog_interval_peak.cpp` | Legacy V1 operation |

## TimeFrame handling

Most transforms do **not** call `setTimeFrame` on their output. TimeFrame
assignment is normally performed by `DataManager::setData` (or
`ElementRegistry` propagation for single-input transforms).

`AnalogIntervalPeak` is an exception. It explicitly attaches a TimeFrame on
the output `DigitalEventSeries` because:

1. **Stored events use analog indices.** Peak times written to storage are
   `TimeFrameIndex` values from the analog series coordinate system.
2. **Binary registry propagation uses input1 only.** `ElementRegistry`
   copies the first input's TimeFrame (`DigitalIntervalSeries`). When analog
   and interval series use different time bases, that would make `view()`
   resolve the wrong `ClockTicks`.
3. **The transform therefore prefers the analog TimeFrame**, falling back to
   the interval TimeFrame only when analog has none.

When committing results through the UI or `SynthesizeData`, still assign the
output to the analog time key so `DataManager` and the transform agree on the
time base.

## Parameters

```cpp
struct AnalogIntervalPeakParams {
    enum class PeakType { maximum, minimum };
    enum class SearchMode { within_intervals, between_starts };

    PeakType peak_type = PeakType::maximum;
    SearchMode search_mode = SearchMode::within_intervals;
};
```

## Usage

### Registry execution

```cpp
auto result = ElementRegistry::instance().executeBinaryContainerTransform<
    DigitalIntervalSeries,
    AnalogTimeSeries,
    DigitalEventSeries,
    AnalogIntervalPeakParams>(
    "AnalogIntervalPeak", intervals, analog, params);
```

## Related transforms

- `AnalogEventThreshold` — threshold crossings on a single `AnalogTimeSeries`
  (does not attach TimeFrame; single-input propagation applies)
